sections.h2: What is Coffee County, Georgia like for a home seller?
sections.html:
Douglas is both the seat and the biggest city of Coffee County, which lies in south Georgia's Wiregrass region. The legislature created the county in 1854. It spans 603 square miles, 575 of them land, and holds three other incorporated cities: Ambrose, Broxton and Nicholls. South Georgia State College, the University System's oldest two-year school, is in Douglas.

The 2020 census found 43,092 people in 15,277 households and a median age of 36.6. Of the 17,331 housing units, 11.9% stood vacant. Among occupied homes, owners held 63.9% and renters 36.1%. Sellers with acreage should look at the land programs described below before they list.

Local landmarks include the Broxton Rocks sandstone outcrops, General Coffee State Park at 1,490 acres, and Mule Day, held the second Saturday in November.

sections.h2: Which Coffee County offices handle property tax?
sections.html:
Two offices share the job. Values and appeals belong to the Coffee County Tax Assessors Office, at 224 West Ashley Street, Suite C, in Douglas. It keeps weekday hours from 8:00 to 5:00 and answers at 912-384-2136, with a separate personal property line, 912-493-1100.

Billing, collection and homestead applications sit with the Tax Commissioner, next door in Suite B at 224 Ashley Street West. Weekday hours run from 8:00 to 4:50, and the phone is (912) 384-4895. Mail goes to P.O. Box 1207, Douglas, GA 31533. Online payment runs through the commissioner's site, which sits on a vendor's platform. Bill questions belong here, because the assessors' page says they establish values only.

Georgia cities levy their own ad valorem tax, and in some counties the Tax Commissioner collects it on the same bill. Ask the Tax Commissioner whether a parcel in Douglas, Broxton, Nicholls or Ambrose gets one bill or two.

sections.h2: What are the key property tax deadlines in Coffee County?
sections.html:
The assessors' page prints the dates owners need most. April 1 closes filing for homestead exemptions, personal property returns and the conservation use, preferential and forest land programs, though those applications are also taken during the appeal window. Eligibility is measured on January 1, when you must still own and live in the home.

Coffee County filing and appeal dates printed by the Tax Assessors Office
ItemDate
Homestead exemption filingJanuary 1 to April 1
Personal property returnApril 1
Conservation use, preferential and forest land applicationsApril 1, or during the appeal window
2026 assessment notices mailedAugust 4, 2026
2026 appeal deadlineSeptember 18, 2026 (passed)

A review of every parcel is also under way, spread over three years, with contract appraisers from GMASS who wear ID badges and drive marked vehicles. The assessors give notice that appraisers will visit parcels sold in the last 12 months or tied to a building permit, a value return, fire damage, demolition or an appeal. Most field visits fall between January 1 and May 1.

sections.h2: How do you appeal a Coffee County assessment?
sections.html:
Forty-five days from the notice date is the rule, and it explains the 2026 window of August 4 to September 18. Owners of real property are urged to use the appeals module on the county's qPublic site, with lobby computers for anyone who prefers to file in person. Personal property appeals go on paper, with a postmark by the deadline if mailed.

The assessors review each appeal first. If they leave the value alone, the file passes to the Board of Equalization for a hearing and decision, and a still-unhappy owner can then go to Superior Court. Arbitration is offered as a substitute for the Board of Equalization hearing. Valid grounds are taxability, value and uniformity with similar properties. The size of the bill is not one of them.

A notice that never arrived is a reason to call the assessors and confirm the mailing address on file, since their page says what they give you then counts as the official notice.

sections.h2: What exemptions and programs does Coffee County list?
sections.html:
Homestead applications go to the Tax Commissioner from January 1 to April 1 of the first year you want the exemption. Approval carries forward every year until ownership changes or you switch to a different kind. The county's exemptions page lists:

  • A standard homestead exemption.
  • A $4,000 exemption for owners 65 or older.
  • An added school tax exemption for owners 62 or older whose household income stays under the limit printed on the page, up to $10,000 of assessed value.
  • A $50,000 exemption for qualifying disabled veterans, extended to an unremarried surviving spouse or minor children.
  • A tax deferral program for homestead owners 62 and older with gross income of $15,000 or less. Deferred tax is due when ownership changes or when the deferred amount plus interest reaches 85% of the property's fair market value.

State law can change those amounts, so confirm each with the Tax Commissioner before relying on it. In years when the legislature funds the Homeowners Tax Relief Grant, it appears as a credit on the bill.

Landowners have their own options. Qualifying agricultural property can be assessed at 30% of fair market value in place of the usual 40%. Conservation use assessment asks for a 10-year covenant and a $10.00 recording fee with the application. Breaking the covenant costs twice the taxes saved, plus 1% monthly interest if the break goes unreported. A buyer who keeps the same use can sign onto the covenant.

sections.h2: When are Coffee County property taxes due and what if they are late?
sections.html:
Unless a local government changes it, the state due date is December 20. A county may choose December 1, November 15 or installment billing instead, so read the date on your Coffee County bill or ask the Tax Commissioner. The state fact sheet says interest does not start until 60 days after the bill's postmark, and penalties may follow.

Tax assessed in error can be refunded if you ask in writing within three years of paying it. Appealed values refund automatically once final. Balances left unpaid can lead to a lien and a tax sale, and a title company will want them cleared at closing.

If the land is in a conservation use covenant, tell your closing attorney, because a sale to a buyer who will change the use can trigger the penalty.

sections.h2: How do property taxes work when you sell a Coffee County house?
sections.html:
The tax follows the January 1 owner, and your sales contract and settlement statement decide how the year is shared. Have the closing attorney request a payoff from the Tax Commissioner, (912) 384-4895, covering any city bill too. Afterward, tell the commissioner so your homestead exemption is dropped, and let the buyer know they must file their own, by April 1.

  • Confirm the current balance and whether a city bill also applies.
  • Ask whether the parcel is in conservation use, since the covenant affects a buyer.
  • Check whether a homestead exemption will need to be dropped.
  • Keep the closing statement as proof that taxes were paid.

Deferred maintenance, tenants or back taxes can slow a conventional sale. A cash buyer who takes the house as-is avoids the lender's appraisal and can close around the payoff.

faqs.q: Which Coffee County office do I call about a tax question?
faqs.a: Bills, payments and homestead filings go to the Tax Commissioner at (912) 384-4895. Values and appeals go to the Tax Assessors Office at 912-384-2136. The assessors only set values, so a bill question gets redirected to the commissioner.

faqs.q: When must a Coffee County homestead exemption be filed?
faqs.a: By April 1, in the first year you want it, and you must own and occupy the home on January 1. The Tax Commissioner takes the application. One filed later generally waits for the next tax year.

faqs.q: Did Coffee County's 2026 appeal window close?
faqs.a: Yes. Notices went out August 4, 2026, and the last day to appeal was September 18, 2026. Real property owners were steered to the qPublic appeals module. Future windows run 45 days from the notice date printed on the notice.

faqs.q: Does Coffee County conservation use transfer to a buyer?
faqs.a: It can. A buyer who keeps the same qualifying use and signs the covenant avoids any penalty. A change of use inside the 10-year period brings twice the taxes saved. Tell your closing attorney if the parcel is enrolled.

faqs.q: How does a Coffee County closing handle the tax bill?
faqs.a: Your proceeds cover the balance, city bill included, and the contract sets each side's share of the year. Ask the Tax Commissioner for a payoff dated to your closing.
